business_problem: Developers were losing time to fragmented knowledge, manual planning, and context switching across tools instead of spending that time on high-leverage engineering work.
solution_summary: Factory built an AI-native command center for software development by embedding OpenAI reasoning models into each phase of the engineering lifecycle. The platform uses o3-mini for codebase exploration and documentation lookup where speed matters, OpenAI o1 for architectural planning and system-level reasoning, and GPT-4o for code generation, editing, and review with lower-latency predicted outputs. Around those models, Factory’s context-first architecture retrieves information from codebases, documentation, and issue-tracking systems so developers can plan, understand dependencies, and act without switching across tools. The company is also experimenting with reinforcement fine-tuning o3-mini for code reranking and lightweight guidance injection to improve compliance. Its long-term direction is to connect reasoning models to source control, project management, team communication, monitoring, and delivery systems so AI can proactively plan, execute, and refine engineering work.

data_flow: Codebase content, documentation, issue-tracker context, and developer tasks are pulled into the Factory Platform. The platform routes exploration to o3-mini, planning to o1, and execution to GPT-4o, then returns code, insights, and workflow actions in one environment instead of multiple disconnected tools.
business_outcome: Factory accelerated feature delivery, cut context switching, increased developer throughput, and created a foundation for more autonomous engineering workflows that can reason over both code and process context.
